relevance_note: One cohort patient carries a germline TNFAIP3 frameshift: 'A variant in the tumor necrosis factor, alpha-induced protein (TNFAIP)3 gene (c.997dupG) resulting in a frameshift (p.A333fs^*2) was found in P10'.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans and fields (no automated table transcription). Scope: this is a 20-patient whole-exome CVID cohort; only P10 carries a TNFAIP3 variant (Table 2). The other 19 patients (variants in NFKB1, STAT3, IL17F, IRAK4, TTC37, DDX41, NLRC3, TNFRSF1A, PLCG2 or none) and the relatives of P2, P3 and P15 have no reported TNFAIP3 variant and were not extracted, by analogy with the rule that papers with no TNFAIP3 carrier leave patient tables empty; a reviewer may prefer all 20 rows. Label: tables use 'P10'; the text also says 'Patient 10'; 'P10' used throughout. Table column headers used: Table 1 'Age at diagnosis' (value 23; unit not printed, read as years since the cohort is adult, ISO P23Y), 'Recurrent infectious manifestations', 'Other conditions', 'Hematology'; Table 2 'ACMG classification' (4 = likely pathogenic, consistent with the abstract and with 'four were classified as likely pathogenic'); Table 4 lab columns. Lab-derived features (IgG, IgA, lymphocyte count) are values interpreted against the reference ranges printed in the Table 4 notes; T-cell, CD8, NK and B-cell counts for P10 are also below the printed ranges but were not extracted as separate features. IgM for P10 is '^*' (no measurement). Treatment: IVIG inferred from the Table 4 cell 'NP (only after IVIG)'; the statement that all but one patient received immunoglobulin substitution does not name the exception, so it was not used. Group statements used: switched memory B cells reduced in all except P15 (observed for P10); ITP only in P17 and P18 and malignancy only in P1, P4, P5, P6, P12, P17 (excluded for P10). Checklist judgements: 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' left not reported because the anemia, thrombocytopenia and pancytopenia are not called autoimmune and the thrombocytopenia is linked to hypersplenism; 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' left not reported because only splenomegaly/hepatosplenomegaly (with portal hypertension and nodular regenerative hyperplasia) is stated, not lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy; 'oral ulcers' left not reported because only 'stomatitis' is stated. The text 'diagnosed with CVID 10 years ago' gives time since diagnosis, not an age, so age at last evaluation is not reported. Country/ancestry not stated (patients are from the Danish CVID cohort at Aarhus University Hospital; that is the place of care, not stated ancestry). Prior report: the paper states the Danish CVID cohort was described previously (ref 2, Westh 2017, cohort-level aggregate data) and that a subgroup was analysed by flow cytometry (ref 8, Kofod-Olsen 2016, 26 patients); it does not say P10 was individually described before. The sentence on the OTU domain and 'severely truncated and rapidly degraded protein' refers to p.A332X from ref 35, not to an assay of P10's variant, so it was not recorded as functional evidence. Protein string kept as printed 'p.A333fs^*2' (the '^' appears to be a conversion artifact of a superscript asterisk). Contradictions/inconsistencies noted (none affect P10's extracted values): DOI contains '2019' while the journal line gives 2020 (2020 used); Results call the NFKB1 variants novel while the Discussion calls them 'previously described'; PLCG2 CADD is 33 in Table 2 but 35 in the text (P18).
